label: copy phase, early recall in long sequences, re-fed j/i/v/h/2 (sparse conjunction)
explanation: Very sparse feature (0.03% of steps). Almost all of it (94% of mass) is in the copy phase, with a little at <DEL>; it essentially never fires in the original phase. It is tied to the input token: j (43% of mass, 14x lift), then i, v, h, and 2. In the copy phase that input is the model own previous output. It is concentrated at recall_idx 2 (61% of mass, so the input is orig(1)) in long sequences (L=9 holds 62% of mass), with a weaker bump at late recall (recall_idx 7-8). It is also biased toward certain output and next-output tokens (n, 2, u / w, e, s) and previous tokens (o, v, n, e). But no conjunction gives useful precision. copy & in_tok in {j,i,v,h,2} covers 89% of mass at 0.4% precision. Adding recall_idx==2, L>=8 and an out_tok set gives dev F1 0.13, and adding a prev_tok set raises it only to 0.19 with recall falling. The feature looks like a sparse joint code over several specific tokens in the hidden state, not a single describable property. Magnitude is fairly flat across quartiles (median 0.12, max 0.24); the top activations are j at recall_idx 2 in L=8-9 sequences. Not checked further.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=j (+5.92), phase=2 & in_tok=i (+4.25), phase=2 & in_tok=v (+4.23), phase=2 & in_tok=h (+3.91), phase=2 & in_tok=2 (+3.64), out_tok=2 (+3.39). Lower it: orig4=j (-2.11), orig1=f (-1.96), orig5=- (-1.84), orig8=- (-1.84).
